 Judgment

This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB referred to as 'the Act', for short) by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 05.02.2022 passed in MVC No.484/2019 by the II-Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Bidar.
2.

3. Appellant is the petitioner and the respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.

4. Facts giving rise to filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 03.05.2019, the petitioner being the driver, he kept the lorry for repair in the garage and to bring the spare parts, the petitioner along with the mechanic Solanki Mangal were going towards Channur from Padmanagar Channur on the motor cycle bearing registration No.AP-01/Q-0628.

The petitioner was a pillion rider and Solanki Mangal was riding the motorcycle on the left side of the road very slowly at that time, one car NC:
2024:KHC-K:3879-DB bearing registration No.TS-19/B-8169 came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent and in a zig zag manner and dashed to the motorcycle.
Due to which, the petitioner sustained injuries.
The criminal case was registered against the driver of car bearing registration No.TS-19/B- 8169.
It is contended that the petitioner was working as a driver and drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and the petitioner was also getting Rs.200/- per day as batta.
Due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, the petitioner has stopped the driving.
Hence, the occupation of the petitioner is nil now.
The petitioner has invested huge amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, the petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation on account of the injuries stained in the road traffic accident.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the claim petition.
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not appear before the Tribunal.

Hence,
they were placed exparte.
Respondent No.3 filed written NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

The driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6.

On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The petitioner, in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW.1 and also examined the employer as PW.2.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner examined the doctor as PW.3 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
The respondents have not led any evidence either oral or documentary.

7. The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on assessment of the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs and ordered that respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally are liable to pay the compensation.
It was ordered that the petitioner is entitled to a total NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB compensation of Rs.11,05,812/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Tribunal directed respondent No.3 to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of the said order.
8. The petitioner, aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
9. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner and also learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company.

Chasmoddin vs Banaiahattem And Ors on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17962489/
3 10.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in order to establish that he was working as driver in Balaji Transport at Tandoor examined the employer of the petitioner as PW.2.
PW.2 has deposed that he was paying salary of Rs.15,000/- per month to the petitioner and Rs.300/- as batta per day.

He further submits that in order to prove the disability examined the Dr.Rajendra NC:
2024:KHC-K:3879-DB Kothari as PW.3 who has issued disability certificate marked as Ex.P11 wherein he has opined that the petitioner is suffering from permanent disability of 60% to the whole body and he cannot drive the vehicle in future.
However, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 40% which is on the lower side.
He also submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the other heads is also on the lower side.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
Hence, on these grounds, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Perused the records and considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB 13.
The point that arises for consideration is in regard to quantum of compensation.
14. It is not in dispute that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.

In order to prove that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced Ex.P1 which is the certified copy of the FIR and certified copy of the charge sheet which is marked as Ex.P3.
The Tribunal placing reliance on Exs.P1 and P3 has rightly recorded finding that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. Insofar as disability:

In order to establish that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability,
the petitioner has examined the Doctor as PW.3 who has examined the petitioner.
After going through the medical record and after examining the petitioner clinically and radiologically, PW.3 found that the petitioner met with an accident on 03.05.2019.

He has opined that the petitioner NC:
2024:KHC-K:3879-DB has suffered traumatic dorsolumar and spine injury as found clinically and readiologically following the accident and there is total motor loss in both lower limbs including hip,
knee, ankle and foot joints that accounts for neurological disability of 50%.

There is sensory loss in the posterior aspect of both lower limbs and patchy loss in remaining limbs that accounts for neurological disability of 20% and he needs assistance of someone for daily duties and to continue physiotherapy that cost about Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month.
With the above finding, the cumulative disability sustained by the petitioner in the accident is 60% to the entire body and permanent in nature and he cannot drive the truck anymore.
Though the doctor has opined the disability at 60%, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 40% which is on the lower side.
16. Considering the evidence of PW.3 and the medical records, we are of the opinion that the disability assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

Thus, we are Chasmoddin vs Banaiahattem And Ors on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17962489/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB of the opinion that the permanent disability suffered by the petitioner has to be considered at 55%.

17. Insofar as quantum of compensation: It is the case of the petitioner that he was working as driver in Balaji Transport of Tandur village and was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and Rs.200/- Batta per day.

In order to substantiate the case, the petitioner has produced salary certificate marked as Ex.P10 which discloses that the petitioner was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/-
per month.

Further, in order to prove the contents of Ex.P10, the petitioner has examined the author of the document i.e., PW.2 who has deposed that the petitioner was working as driver in Balaji Transport in Tandur and he was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and Rs.200/- batta per day.
Without considering the salary certificate produced by the petitioner at Ex.P10, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month which is on the lower side.
Considering the salary certificate produced at Ex.P10, we assess the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.

The petitioner is also entitled for addition of 40% towards future prospect in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Erudhaya Priya Vs.
State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. reported 2020 SCC Online SC 601.

sentences.text: Considering the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- and the other factors as stated supra, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.22,17,600/- (Rs.15,000/- + 40% =Rs.21,000 x 12 x 16 x 55%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and also the evidence of PW.3, we reassess the compensation awarded under the following heads:
Particulars Compensation Compensation awarded by awarded by the Tribunal this Court Loss of future income Rs.8,44,800/- Rs.22,17,600/- Pain and suffering Rs.75,000/- Rs.1,50,000/- Medical expenses Rs.26,012/- Rs.26,012/- Loss of income during Rs.40,000/- Rs.63,000/-
laid-up period Food and Rs.20,000/- Rs.40,000/-

5 nourishment,
conveyance and attendant charges.
Loss of future amenity Rs.1,00,000/- Rs.2,00,000/-
 Total: Rs.11,05,812/- Rs.26,96,612/-
20.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.26,96,612/- as against Rs.11,05,812/-.
21.

In view of the above discussion, we proceed to pass the following:
- 13 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3879-DB  ORDER  i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award passed by  the Tribunal in MVC No.484/2019  dated 05.02.2022 is modified.
The  petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.15,90,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization.
iii. Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
The Tribunal is directed to release the enhanced compensation amount in favour of the petitioner.
